overall.verdict: Low Interaction Risk — Minor Notes Only
overall.summary: Taking metformin and lisinopril together is generally considered low risk, but the combination can make your blood sugar drop lower than expected. Watch for signs of low blood sugar and let your doctor know if they occur. Overall, the regimen is safe for most adults when monitored properly.

context_advice: As a standard adult, you can usually take metformin and lisinopril together, but keep an eye on low blood‑sugar symptoms and discuss any concerns with your doctor or pharmacist.

drugs.name: lisinopril

label_hits.text: 7.2 Antidiabetics Concomitant administration of lisinopril and antidiabetic medicines (insulins, oral hypoglycemic agents) may cause an increased blood-glucose-lowering effect with risk of hypoglycemia.

explanation.why: Both drugs lower blood sugar, so using them together can increase the blood‑glucose‑lowering effect and raise the chance of hypoglycemia.
explanation.timing: Check your blood glucose more often, especially when you first start both medicines or if doses are changed, and let your doctor know any low readings.
